articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft drops 167 patches including a SharePoint zero-day and Windows Defender's 'BlueHammer' flaw. Chrome chimes in with its fourth vuln of the year because apparently security is just a suggestion.

articles.title: Phishing Campaign Hits 80+ Orgs Using SimpleHelp and ScreenConnect RMM Tools
articles.summary: CISA confirms attackers are exploiting a critical cPanel bug affecting millions of sites, with ransomware already hitting victims. When your hosting control panel becomes their control panel, you're gonna have a bad time.

articles.title: US CISA adds ‘insane’ Linux Copy Fail flaw to watch list
articles.summary: CISA adds Linux root access bug CVE-2026-31431 to the KEV catalog after active exploitation detected. Because apparently someone figured out how to make sudo even more dangerous.

articles.title: Germany Doxes “UNKN,” Head of RU Ransomware Gangs REvil, GandCrab
articles.summary: Russian military intelligence hacked routers to mass-harvest Microsoft Office tokens from unsuspecting users. Your ancient Linksys just became Moscow's favorite data buffet.

articles.title: ADT data breach exposes customer information
articles.summary: Cybersecurity firm Trellix admits unauthorized access to portions of their source code repository. The irony is so thick you could cut it with a zero-day exploit.

articles.title: Silver Fox Springs Tax-Themed Attacks on Orgs in India, Russia
articles.summary: Public records laws exposed ALPR surveillance abuse, so naturally states want to block transparency efforts. Because nothing says 'we're the good guys' like hiding how you spy on citizens.

articles.title: Open Records Laws Reveal ALPRs’ Sprawling Surveillance. Now States Want to Block What the Public Sees.
articles.summary: Utah's anti-VPN law goes into effect, because apparently privacy is now illegal in the beehive state. Time to dust off those Tor bridges, folks.

articles.title: Week in review: High-severity LPE vulnerability in the Linux kernel, cPanel 0-day exploited for months
articles.summary: Citizen Lab exposes sophisticated telecom surveillance campaigns linking attack traffic to mobile operator infrastructure. Your phone company isn't just dropping calls anymore—they're dropping your privacy too.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider member 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud after SMS phishing campaigns. Another script kiddie learns that 'for the lulz' isn't a valid legal defense.

articles.title: EFF Submission to UK Consultation on Digital ID
articles.summary: Germany unmasks 'UNKN', the elusive Russian behind REvil and GandCrab ransomware empires. Turns out 31-year-old Daniil Shchukin wasn't as unknown as he thought—whoops.
